# farmout

> farmout puts the AI subscriptions a developer already pays for to work together: Codex (Codex CLI on a ChatGPT account), Gemini and other models through the Antigravity CLI (agy, on a Google account), GitHub Copilot CLI, a second Claude Code account, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, OpenRouter). It drives each vendor's official CLI in its documented non-interactive mode, logged in as the user: no API keys, no proxy, no token extraction. It is a CLI and an MCP server in standard-library Python 3.9+ with zero dependencies, MIT licensed. Workers are read-only by default; writing needs --write, or --isolate (a private git worktree whose result comes back as a patch).

Main commands:
- `farmout review`: every worker reviews the uncommitted change (or --staged, or --base <ref>) in parallel, read-only. Findings are merged across models with agreement counts; findings citing a file or line that doesn't exist are dropped. `--min-agree N` and `--fail-on high|medium|low` make it a gate (also as a git hook: `farmout hook install`).
- `farmout race "<task>" --test "<cmd>"`: every worker attempts the task in its own git worktree; passing tests win, then the smallest diff, then the fastest. `farmout apply` (or `--pr`) lands the winner; `farmout undo` takes it back.
- `farmout run <worker> "<prompt>" -n <name>`, `farmout send <name> "<msg>"`, `farmout fork`: named sessions resumed through each CLI's own session id (claude --resume, codex exec resume, copilot --session-id, agy --conversation), so the model remembers earlier turns. Messages to a busy session queue; `farmout attach` watches from any terminal. Sessions are found by name, so a renamed or moved project keeps its conversations.
- `farmout fork <name> --at <turn>` branches a conversation off any turn, on any worker or model (`-w worker[:model]`); `farmout tree` draws each conversation as a graph of its branches, and `farmout ui` opens them all full-screen in the terminal to read, continue or branch from any turn (`farmout ui --web`: the same in a local browser page, 127.0.0.1 with a key per run).
- `farmout pipe run <pipeline>`: TOML or JSON pipelines whose stages start when the previous one ends, with gates (tests, agree >= N, high == 0, contains "TEXT"), approvals, foreach fan-out and resume. Built in: `fix` (review, fix what 2+ models agree on, review the fix) and `spec`.
- `farmout ask "<question>"` (`--debate` lets each model read the others and answer again), `farmout bench` (replays recent bug fixes from the user's git history and scores each model), `farmout fix-pr <n>` (PR comments and failing checks become a race), `farmout stats`, `farmout status --line`, `farmout ls --watch`.
- Skills in the SKILL.md format Claude Code, Codex and Copilot share; hooks on farmout's own events (SessionStart, MessageReceived, TaskStart, TaskEnd, StageEnd, PipelineEnd); a store whose entries are pinned file by file by SHA-256.
- As an MCP server (`farmout mcp`), any MCP client (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Copilot CLI) can be the head: tools delegate, send, sessions and pipeline. A Claude Code plugin adds /farmout:review, /farmout:race, /farmout:ask and a read guard that delegates big reads.

Measured (bench/README.md in the repository, raw outputs committed, 2026-11-17):
- 32 bugs (23 planted in five realistic changes, 9 real BugsInPy regressions): every one flagged by at least 3 of the 4 models, 27 by all four. Per reviewer: Antigravity 32, Claude (Sonnet) 32, Copilot 30, Codex 29.
- No recall gain over the best single model given room: Claude (Sonnet) alone found all 23 planted bugs when allowed 30 findings. Four reviewers covered more only under a 10-finding cap (17 vs 10 of 23).
- Delegating the reading of three arXiv papers (43 pages) from a Claude head to Antigravity: 59% fewer head tokens and 74% lower head cost, same answers, 62s instead of 13s.
- A four-model review of a real change takes about a minute end to end.

Settings (user and per repository) can only narrow: allowed workers intersect, write and web access are off if either file says so, `redact = true` strips credentials from briefs. A worker that hits its usage limit is skipped until the reset time it reports, and tasks fall back to the next worker.

Install: `pipx install git+https://github.com/JayPokale/farmout`, then `farmout doctor --live`. Claude Code plugin: `claude plugin install farmout --marketplace JayPokale/farmout`. Linux tested, macOS untested, no Windows before v1.0.
